description: RGB-split + horizontal pixel shift + brief noise burst between clips. Digital horror aesthetic — 'the simulation is glitching'. More aggressive than static-noise-transition (which is purely analog VHS noise).
audio_recipe: acrossfade 0.3s on base + optional bit-crushed glitch SFX (drone-tension.mp3 with chorus + bitcrush effect) at volume 0.40, peak at glitch_start + 0.1s.
audio_processing_hint: For full glitch effect, pre-process drone-tension.mp3 with ffmpeg -af 'chorus=0.7:0.9:55:0.4:0.25:2,aresample=8000,aresample=44100' to bitcrush.
use_cases: Liminal-space transition with 'something is broken' cue
Memory corruption with technological flavor (vs. VHS = analog)
avoid_for: More than 2x per reel — exhausts impact
hyperframes_alternative: CSS+GSAP: tween `filter:hue-rotate(0deg) → hue-rotate(45deg)` + `transform:translate(0,0) → translate(8px,-4px)` over 0.3s; or use canvas RGB-channel split with requestAnimationFrame.
validated_against_canonical_refs: N/A — digital-horror sub-genre not in F1 set
validated_notes: Use simplified recipe (hlslice xfade) as default — full RGB-split filtergraph is heavier compute and only worth it on flagship climax cuts. Manual QA per video.
